message.content: {"summary":"A strong submission overall. Your modular monolith recommendation in Q2 is excellent, and Q3(a)(b) show correct working. To reach higher marks: make Q1's availability response measure measurable, fix the Q3(c) series calculation, apply CAP correctly in Q5, add a negative consequence in Q6, and trim Q2 to 150 words.","next_steps":["Rewrite the availability response measure in Q1 as a measurable target, e.g. '99.9% uptime measured monthly', and check both scenarios' response measures are quantified.","In Q3(c), multiply the order-path availability (0.998001) by the new payment-pair availability (0.999975) to get ≈99.80% end-to-end, giving ≈1.5 h downtime per month; show the working.","In Q5, restate CAP correctly: during a partition you must choose C or A, so frame the payment choice as CP (sacrificing availability during the partition), and add a technique for the other case.","Add at least one negative consequence to your Q6 ADR, e.g. delayed order confirmation or added queue infrastructure complexity.","Trim Q2 to within 150 words while keeping both scenario-specific trade-offs and the acknowledged downside."],"criteria":{"C1":"You chose suitable attributes (performance, availability) with good scenario justification and six-part scenarios. To reach Excellent, both response measures must be measurable — 'stay up most of the time' is not. Replace it with a quantified target such as a percentage uptime over a stated period, and double-check the other scenario's measures too.","C2":"Excellent work. Your modular monolith recommendation is justified with two scenario-specific trade-offs (five-developer team overhead; problems traced to the single VM and deployment process) and you explicitly acknowledge the downside of independent scaling. This fully meets the Excellent level — keep this standard for future justifications.","C3":"Parts (a) and (b) are correct with working shown. In part (c) you report 99.9975% (the payment-pair availability) as the end-to-end availability. The method requires multiplying the series: 0.998001 × 0.999975 ≈ 99.80%, giving ≈1.5 h downtime per month, not 0.018 h. Fixing this single slip moves you toward Excellent.","C4":"You correctly named and explained the circuit breaker (Closed/Open/Half-Open) and applied it to the outage with a sensible user-facing message. For the full 5 marks, add an explicit drawback or tuning consideration — e.g. payments fail while the breaker is Open, or how the threshold should be tuned to avoid tripping on transient faults.","C5":"Your choices (Redis TTL cache, idempotency keys) are concrete and reasonable, but CAP is misapplied: you claim choosing both consistency and availability and giving up partition tolerance. During a partition only C or A can be kept — frame payments as CP, sacrificing availability during the partition. Correcting this and ensuring a technique for each case reaches Excellent.","C6":"Your ADR has scenario-specific Context, Decision and Consequences, but the consequences are one-sided — only benefits are listed. Add at least one negative consequence, such as eventual notification delay or added message-queue infrastructure complexity. With that, all three sections plus balanced consequences meet the Excellent level.","C7":"Your writing is clear, headings are used correctly, and IEEE citations and a reference list are present. However, Question 2 clearly exceeds the 150-word limit, which prevents the Excellent level. Keep answers within limits while preserving the quality of your trade-off discussion."}}
